Construct the survey-intensity field

Source: R/fn_survey.R
survey_field.Rd

Bundles the records, their per-record weights and the bandwidth into a lightweight survey_field object that eval_survey and survey_raster evaluate. Nothing is discretised here.

Usage

survey_field(
  coords,
  species,
  sigma = 100,
  record_type = NULL,
  plot_types = "Plot",
  plot_weight = 1,
  basis = NULL,
  basis_weights = c(PRESERVED_SPECIMEN = 1.5),
  weights = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  min_records = 5,
  p = 0.95,
  damp = 1,
  trunc = 4
)

Arguments

coords

two-column matrix/data.frame of record coordinates (metres).

species

vector of species labels (one per record).

sigma

kernel bandwidth \(\sigma\) in map units (metres), the radius over which one record counts ground as surveyed (default 100).

record_type

optional per-record label splitting the two detection processes. Records whose label is in plot_types are treated as vegetation plots - a complete floristic inventory at one spot (FIA, AIM, VegBank, ...), so absence there is strong evidence. Plot records are deduplicated by coordinate (the many species-rows of one plot are a single survey event, not many) and each surviving plot point carries plot_weight; they are also held out of the opportunistic frequency counts. NULL treats every record as opportunistic. See guess_record_type to derive this from a dataset/origin column.

plot_types

labels in record_type that mark a plot (default "Plot", matched case-insensitively).

plot_weight

per-record weight for a deduplicated plot point (default 1 - the ceiling of the opportunistic weights, which sit in \((0, 1]\); raise it to let plots dominate further).

basis

optional per-record basisOfRecord labels (as from gbif_records); used to up-weight deliberate collections.

basis_weights

named multipliers applied per opportunistic record by its basis (default c(PRESERVED_SPECIMEN = 1.5) - a herbarium specimen marks survey effort ~50% more strongly than an iNaturalist photo). Any basis not named here is neutral (1); the \(n_j \ge 5\) floor keeps even a boosted opportunistic weight below the plot ceiling.

weights

optional per-species weights: a data.frame as returned by survey_weights (matched on species), a named numeric vector, or NULL to compute them from domain/min_records/p/damp. Applied to the opportunistic records only.

domain, min_records, p, damp

passed to survey_weights when weights is NULL. Records of any species absent from the weight set - below the floor, or omitted by the caller - are dropped from the field.

trunc

kernel support in units of \(\sigma\) (default 4).

Value

an object of class survey_field: a list with coords, species (plot points labelled "__plot__"), per-record w, sigma, trunc, the opportunistic per-species weights table and plot_weight.

See also

eval_survey, survey_raster
